sentences.text: Most species of Phoebodus are known only from isolated tricuspid teeth.
The genus Phoebodus was first described by St. John and Worthen in 1875.
New fossil material of Phoebodus saidselachus was described from the Devonian strata of eastern Anti-Atlas, Morocco, by Klug et al. in 2026.
The teeth of Phoebodus are morphologically similar to those of frilled sharks and designed for grasping prey.
Phoebodus likely consumed small prey items that could be swallowed whole.
Representatives of the genus Phoebodus were certainly predatory animals, given the sharp morphology of their teeth.
The long body of Phoebodus saidelachus suggests it may have been a slow hunter that swallowed prey whole and held it with numerous three-pointed teeth.
Phoebodus is classified as a genus containing multiple species.
Phoebodus belongs to the class Chondrichthyes, which includes cartilaginous fish.
Phoebodus is placed in the extinct family Phoebodontidae.
Phoebodus lived during the middle to late Devonian periods and is found worldwide.
The time range for Phoebodus spans from the Givetian to the Norian, approximately 387.95 to 205.7 million years ago.
It is unclear exactly how Phoebodus hunted or what specific prey it consumed.
